Recently, one of my friends has been bringing his dad along wherever we go. We've been to clubs, and this guy's dad comes along. I told my friends I don't mind them coming over so we can all drink, and one by one, they come into my house, followed by their dads. This specific day was when I introduced that group to my current girlfriend, and she was really creeped out. She said he cornered her and forced her to have a conversation about cooking and different dishes for like half an hour. The point is, when I hang out with all my friends in their early 20s, I don't exactly want to hang out with a dude in his late 40s. He's not a bad guy, but he gets drunk like he's one of the boys and engages in locker room talk about women who are our age. I think it's really disturbing. I've asked some of the guys who are his sons about it, and weirdly, they think it's cool he hangs out with them and considers him one of the boys. Apparently, he had his kids really young and was married already in his early 20s and didn't have the opportunity to get drunk and party with his friends. So now he does it with his son and his friends. Next time this group hits me up, I really want to ask if his dad will be there. I love my friends and still want to hang out with them, but his dad being around ALL THE TIME is too much. I get if we're drinking at his house and wants to hang out, but going out with us or coming to MY house when I didn't know he was coming is a problem. So, is it right or wrong for me to ask my friend if his dad is going to be there before I agree to hang out with them? I think it's a bit tricky because I value my friendships, but I also have my own boundaries and comfort levels. I don't want to make my friend feel bad or like I'm rejecting him, but I also don't want to be in situations where his dad is around all the time, especially if it makes me or my girlfriend uncomfortable. Maybe I should consider how to approach the conversation in a way that's respectful and clear about my boundaries without blaming or criticizing my friend or his dad. It's important to communicate my feelings honestly but also to show understanding of why his dad wants to hang out with us. I wonder if other people have been in similar situations and how they handled it. It might help to think about what's important to me in friendships and how to maintain those relationships while also taking care of my own needs and comfort. Overall, I think it's okay to set boundaries, but I need to do it in a way that's considerate and respectful to everyone involved. I don't want to hurt anyone's feelings, but I also don't want to compromise my own comfort and well-being.
